findings: styleMap tracks previously supplied keys, removes keys that disappear or become nullish, and writes each currently supplied key on updates; it does not loop over every possible CSS property to clear unlisted names.
styleMap writes inline CSS, not house component properties/tokens, so it supplies an ownership pattern rather than a drop-in house helper.

Ordinary Lit property bindings compare with prior bound values; live() explicitly compares against current DOM values. The house helper must document whether it reasserts its controlled values, rather than silently claim all Lit bindings do this.
The existing shared/state.ts re-exports TanStack batch; use and verify it for multiple canonical input writes rather than add a state engine.
Existing bind(field) uses a public AsyncDirective and reasserts its supplied field values/errors during render; it does not implement style ownership.
Inspector read-only versus editing capability is explicitly unresolved. Any future editing must account for helper-controlled properties being reasserted or retained under the upcoming choice.
Three-field ownership/batching fixture passes all 19 assertions in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit; an unbatched control demonstrates a subscriber observing a partly updated pair.
Before the second answer, reasserting current inputs on each helper render was tested as a proposal. Peter then selected it explicitly as C-STYLE-05.
C-STYLE-04 and C-STYLE-05 are selected by Peter; the existing prototype's controlled reassertion test now verifies the selected outcome. No code change or repeat run was needed after that answer.

proposal.question: Should the helper manage only the settings supplied through it, or become the sole input for all supported CSS styling properties on that element?
proposal.recommendation: Manage only supplied settings and clear ones it previously managed when removed; preserve unrelated independently supplied properties. Keep overlapping settings together. Exact competing-writer/lifecycle details remain to complete.
proposal.status: Peter selected Only supplied settings (Recommended), C-STYLE-04.

testLimits: Reassertion after external writes was a proposal when tested and is now selected as C-STYLE-05.
Three scalar fields and global registry; no complete responsive/final type validation.
Clearing a key is tested; removing the helper expression itself has a separate lifecycle/ownership contract.
The unbatched comparison deliberately exposes an intermediate subscriber state; its assertion passing is evidence against unbatched publication, not approval of that behavior.
Batching checks cover coherent notifications for the tested writes, not exception rollback, every subscriber or all future converters.

The fixture's acquired background-color input clears to undefined/CSS defaults on removal; this is not approval of multiple concurrent writers for the same property or automatic restoration of an old input snapshot.

nextChoice.question: If outside code changes a helper-managed property, should the next parent helper render reassert its supplied value even when that supplied value has not changed?
nextChoice.recommendation: Reassert helper inputs on each render, following styleMap and the inspected @lit/react wrapper; no continuous interception of direct writes.
nextChoice.alternative: Only write when the helper input changes, like ordinary Lit property bindings, allowing outside writes to persist between input changes.
nextChoice.inspectorDependency: Do not decide inspector editing now; return to this controlled-input behavior if editing is included.

decisions.selected: The Lit helper manages the styling settings supplied through it and clears previously managed settings when removed. Unrelated independently supplied attributes/properties remain intact. Overlapping settings stay together in the helper.
decisions.limits: Same-key external-write behavior is subsequently selected as C-STYLE-05. Exact name/types, removal of the helper expression itself, broader competing-writer rules, scoped registries and full responsive/property coverage remain.

decisions.selected: Reapply supplied helper-managed values on each parent/helper template render, even when the supplied values have not changed. Direct external property writes update canonical state immediately and remain effective until a later helper render. Persistent changes belong in helper inputs.
decisions.basis: Peter's explicit answer after comparison with Lit styleMap, ordinary property bindings and the tested React wrapper.
decisions.limits: No continuous interception or automatic rollback of property writes. Inspector editing capability remains a later decision; retained-value behavior after removing the helper expression itself is still separate.

next: Complete helper-expression removal/lifecycle ownership and final name/types; inspect scoped registries/adopted documents, then finish responsive/token/density contracts. Do not re-ask supplied-key ownership or next-render reassertion. Inspector editing remains a later choice with this dependency.

reproduction.notes: Uses the saved compiled Capturing base and a three-field scratch subclass. The ownership harness was bundled without a new Lit-compiler transform or strict helper type check; earlier compiled lifecycle evidence remains distinct. Temporary paths and ports may need recreation.
